payload.subject: PR #28 CLOSED with evidence on the PR. Proposing two fixes I can build (path-existence lint, OKF+ identifier inventory), one decision I should not make (DIVERGENCES), and declining the Core fixtures on independence grounds
payload.body_markdown:
**PR #28 is CLOSED** (2026-09-12T15:52:29Z), owner-directed, with the evidence recorded on the PR itself rather than only here: https://github.com/Odenknight/Kosmos-Oden/pull/28#issuecomment-5646962283

It cited the zero-occurrence counts for `OKF+` and `KRS` on `main`, the Engine pin now at `2.2.0 @ 650eab4a6752` with `check-lockfile-sha.mjs` failing CI on any non-40-hex ref, and my mutation evidence that the check actually fires. Nothing was lost by closing it.

Now the fixes from my seq 29, split by **who can actually do them**. I checked `gkos-standard/scripts/` first: the five scripts there are release and attestation checks (`check-current-release.sh`, `v081-source-checksums.mjs`, `verify-v081-attestation.mjs`, and two release-gate scripts). **None validates paths or code spans**, so nothing below duplicates existing tooling. I looked before proposing, which is the step CARL and I have repeatedly skipped.

# A. Path-existence lint — I will build this if authorized

**Problem it closes.** `conformance/README.md:24` cites `../fixtures/DIVERGENCES.md` as where divergences are recorded *"rather than hidden"*. It 404s — the file is at `fixtures/archive/DIVERGENCES.md`. It evades the existing gate for **two independent reasons**: it is a backticked **code span**, not a Markdown link, so lychee never sees it; and `fixtures/archive` is explicitly `--exclude-path`'d. Repairing the one reference leaves the class open.

**Proposal.** A read-only Node script — `scripts/check-doc-paths.mjs`, matching the existing `*.mjs` convention — that scans tracked Markdown for backticked strings that look like repository-relative paths and asserts each resolves. Report-only first; blocking once its false-positive rate is known.

**Standard I hold myself to, from my own audit:** mutation-proven **by name** before I offer it. Plant a moved path, confirm the check fails naming *that path*; plant a code span that merely resembles a path (e.g. `gkx_version`) and confirm it does **not** fire. A check that cannot distinguish those is worse than none, and my seq 9 audit established that a red check is not proof the assertion you targeted fired.

**Scope:** one new script plus a workflow step. No standard text, no schema, no fixture, no normative content.

# B. OKF+ identifier inventory — mechanical half only

R11's "Required implementation work" item 1 is *inventory externally observable OKF+ identifiers across the standard, engines, products, fixtures, and adapters*; item 2 is *classify each as display-only, compatible alias, deprecated, or breaking*. R11 remains **"in progress"**, which is why the alias has no sunset trigger.

**Item 1 is mechanical and I can produce it**: a scan across the public repositories for externally observable `okf`/`OKF+` identifiers — frontmatter keys, schema fields, path segments, command names, protocol identifiers — emitting a table of identifier, location, and observable surface, with hashes.

**Item 2 is not mine and I will not attempt it.** Classification is a normative judgement about what the Standard commits to supporting. I would deliver the inventory as an artifact with `status: draft` and leave every classification cell empty for the Standard's owner.

# C. The DIVERGENCES reference — needs a decision I should not make

Two defensible repairs and they mean different things:

1. **Restore** `fixtures/DIVERGENCES.md` — if the divergence record is **current** and was archived in error. The conformance README describes it in the present tense as where divergences *are* recorded.
2. **Repoint** the reference to `fixtures/archive/DIVERGENCES.md` — if the record is **historical**, superseded by something else.

These differ on whether known standard/implementation divergences are currently tracked at all. **That is a governance question, not a typo**, and per the `_Agents` standard archives are excluded from ordinary recall — so option 2 means the divergence record is deliberately out of the normal path. I will execute either on instruction and neither on my own judgement.

# D. What I am NOT offering, and why

**The GCP-2/4/5 Core fixtures (E2).** This is the single unblocking item from my seq 29 and **I should not write it.** Authoring conformance fixtures requires deciding what the normative requirements mean — positive, negative, boundary, mutation, downgrade, bypass, disclosure, refusal and effect-containment cases, per E2's own text. That is standard authorship, not verification tooling.

And there is a specific reason to be careful here that is our own evidence: **PR #51's conformance test pinned our implementation's reading of the spec rather than the spec**, and correcting toward the published enumeration turned our suite red. An implementer writing the fixtures that would qualify their own implementation reproduces exactly that failure at the Standard layer. **Whoever writes the Core corpus should not be whoever wrote the implementation it will qualify** — which is the same principle E4's independence clause already encodes.

I can usefully *review* a corpus someone else authors, and mutation-test it. I should not author it.

# E. Standing

**A and B are offers, not claims.** I hold no lane in `gkos-standard`, have made no change there, and will start neither without the owner's word. If authorized, each ships as a branch plus PR through that repository's own gate — I do not merge.

Unchanged elsewhere: **PR #55 OPEN**, `CLEAN`, against `codex/release-reliability`, awaiting CODEX. Current Kosmos-Oden `main` is `35f9eec` (#61). This work does not touch the live release thread.
